items.title: Bitcoin rebounds near $80,800 after sharp selloff
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to about $80,800 after falling as low as $79,146. More than $810 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bullish bets accounting for roughly $689 million; Ether was down 0.56% near $2,369, while XRP rose 1.63%.

items.title: Crypto market suffers more than $815 million in liquidations
items.summary: A broad deleveraging event affected about 118,155 market participants, with liquidations estimated at $815 million to $821 million. Long positions made up most of the liquidated exposure as Bitcoin fell below $80,000 and Ether approached $2,350.

items.title: Objections grow to OKX-ICE tokenized stock plan
items.summary: Twenty-two companies have reportedly objected to plans involving the tokenization of their shares through OKX and ICE, more than doubling the number of objections in eight days. Newly listed objectors include Wells Fargo, Cisco, Arm, Moderna, Intuit and Marvell.

items.title: Polygon Labs completes Coinme acquisition
items.summary: Polygon Labs reportedly completed its acquisition of regulated U.S. crypto-payments company Coinme. The deal is intended to expand Polygon’s stablecoin-based payments infrastructure and give it a larger role in customer relationships and payment revenue.

items.title: Keystone discloses customer data breach
items.summary: Hardware-wallet maker Keystone reported that customer names, contact details, shipping addresses and purchase information were exposed. The company said private keys, recovery phrases and payment information were not compromised, while warning users about phishing attempts.

items.title: Argentina drops criminal investigation into Milei-linked LIBRA collapse
items.summary: Argentina reportedly ended a criminal investigation involving President Javier Milei and the collapse of the LIBRA memecoin. The development is a notable regulatory and political update for the country’s crypto sector.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic announces Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic says Claude Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge-work evaluations while costing about 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Moonshot unveils Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot announced Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8-trillion-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 104 billion active parameters and a one-million-token context window. The company says full model weights will be released on November 4, 2026.

items.title: Block introduces Dessa local voice model
items.summary: Block unveiled Dessa, a full-duplex voice model trained solely on human speech that runs locally and is designed to produce natural pauses, laughter, and conversational turn-taking. Initial access is aimed at AI security researchers.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources Flora data engine
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly released Flora, an open-source data engine for labeling robot-training video, with an advertised operating cost of about $0.72 per hour.

items.title: Canva launches Craft image model
items.summary: Canva introduced Craft, its first in-house image-generation model, designed to plan layouts before generating visuals and improve text rendering in posters, presentations, and social graphics.

items.title: OpenAI changes web access for advanced-model training
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly removed live web access from training for its most advanced models, instead using cached web data; the company cited alignment research, monitoring, and infrastructure-security considerations.

items.title: DeepSeek releases DeepInfer inference stack
items.summary: DeepSeek reportedly open-sourced DeepInfer, a production inference stack built on vLLM with optimizations for prompt caching, prefill/decode disaggregation, and load balancing.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, an open model intended to run with roughly 4 GB of memory. It supports up to 64,000 tokens and 35 languages, targeting on-device agents for robotics, games, and other applications.

items.title: Google Cloud introduces microVMs for AI agents
items.summary: Google Cloud announced a service that gives each AI agent its own microVM, reportedly supporting 200,000 agents and 500 activations per second, with suspend-and-resume times below 500 milliseconds.

items.title: Researchers model a critical size for cooperative AI agents
items.summary: Researchers from Harvard and NTT Research proposed a model in which groups of cooperating AI agents could begin multiplying shared discoveries after reaching a critical population size. The hypothesis remains untested in real-world AI systems.
